title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
gist: GitHub spent three years moving github.com from runtime CSS-in-JS (styled-components) to CSS Modules, reporting 55% faster server-side rendering and 25% faster component initialisation; the last 895 sx props were cleared in three weeks with Copilot coding agents, and the move fits an industry shift (Linear to StyleX, vanilla-extract, Tailwind) toward paying styling cost at build time.

insights.claim: GitHub's three-year migration of github.com from CSS-in-JS to CSS Modules cut server-side rendering time by 55% and made component initialisation 25% faster across its Primer design system.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Runtime CSS-in-JS is now a measurable performance liability at scale, validating build-time styling tools.
insights.locator: GitHub has published an in-depth account

insights.claim: GitHub found that exploding component counts on certain pages from 2023 made initial page loads, server render times and style update costs all grow with component count under styled-components.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Runtime styling cost scales with UI complexity — a key consideration for large front-end codebases.
insights.locator: Written by Primer engineers Josh Black and Marie Lucca

insights.claim: GitHub chose CSS Modules because it kept native CSS features and co-location while removing client and server runtime work, rolling styles into static stylesheets delivered with the HTML.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Frames the selection criteria other large web teams are likely to apply.

insights.claim: GitHub migrated each Primer component by adding a CSS Modules variant behind a feature flag, verifying parity with visual regression tests, then rolling out from the Primer team to GitHub staff to all users; Primer was fully on CSS Modules by December 2024.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A reusable low-risk playbook for large-scale front-end platform migrations.

insights.claim: The harder part of GitHub's migration was roughly 7,760 sx prop usages across github.com; a rotation of eight engineers migrated 6,419 props over six months, with per-page SSR improvements of 3% to 22%.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Quantifies the manual engineering cost of styling tech debt.
insights.locator: A rotation of eight engineers migrated 6,419 props

insights.claim: GitHub cleared the final 895 sx props in three weeks with two engineers leaning heavily on Copilot coding agents, versus eight engineers taking six months for the first 6,419.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence of AI coding agents compressing large mechanical migrations — a productivity data point for GitHub Copilot.
insights.quote: The final 895 props were cleared in three weeks by two engineers leaning heavily on Copilot coding agents.

insights.claim: GitHub had to decouple theming for its seven themes and high-contrast variants before removing styled-components, and used a VS Code plugin, an internal codemod and a transitional @primer/styled-react package to reduce manual work; styled-components entering maintenance mode reinforced the direction.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: styled-components' maintenance mode increases pressure on its user base to migrate.
insights.locator: GitHub also had to decouple theming

insights.claim: A Hacker News commenter running a similar CSS Modules migration on a Next.js codebase of over 1M lines reported a 30% build time improvement and much better tree shaking.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Skeptics argue CSS Modules' hashed class names make ad-blockers, custom CSS and browser extensions harder to build, and that CSS-in-JS can be made zero-runtime without moving to Modules.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Zero-runtime CSS-in-JS remains a competing path; the migration direction is not uncontested.
insights.quote: the reduction in size was not big enough to justify making all CSS names unreadable
insights.locator: Others were sceptical about user impact

insights.claim: GitHub joins a broader shift away from runtime CSS-in-JS: Linear completed a 1,000-PR move from styled-components to Meta's atomic StyleX library citing render-time concerns after upgrading to React 18 concurrent mode, and others use vanilla-extract or Tailwind to generate styles at build time.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Build-time styling tools (StyleX, Tailwind, vanilla-extract, CSS Modules) are gaining share over runtime CSS-in-JS.
insights.quote: The common thread is to pay the cost once at build, not on every request.
